chapter_title: The Ubik Commercial and the Revelation of Reality
summary: Joe's apartment has regressed to 1939-era fixtures: wood stove, Victrola, pre-World War II furniture. A television broadcast shows Runciter's funeral in Des Moines, but then the TV switches on by itself and plays a Ubik commercial featuring Runciter, who explains that the decay is normal to half-life and that Ubik can reverse it. Joe receives a free sample by mail—but it's a jar of liver and kidney balm from 1908, not a spray can. Joe drives a 1939 LaSalle to an airfield, charters a Curtiss-Wright biplane, and trades the mysterious elixir bottle (which contains gold flakes) for passage to Des Moines. The chapter establishes that Joe is physically regressing through time, and that the world he inhabits is actively devolving.

themes: The regression of technology and civilization
The loss of modern comfort and capability
Time as a tangible force rather than an abstraction
The persistence of commercial logic even in death
